text: People have different opinions about the best age to start school. Some think that children should begin formal lessons at a very young age, while others believe that they should wait until they are older. In this essay, I will discuss both views and explain why I support the second one.

Those who support early education argue that young children learn very quickly. If a child starts learning letters and numbers at the age of four, he or she may find it easier to read and write later. In addition, a good teacher can notice problems in the first years and help the child at once. Moreover, early school helps parents who work, because their children are safe and are learning at the same time. Some studies also show that children who attend nursery school are better at making friends.

However, I believe that children should not start formal education too early. Young children need time to play, because play helps them to develop their imagination and their social skills. If they have to sit at a desk for many hours, they may become tired and lose interest in learning. For example, in Finland, children begin school at seven, but their results are among the best in the world. This shows that an early start is not necessary for success. Children who play a lot also learn to share, to solve problems and to cooperate with others.

In conclusion, early education has some benefits, especially for working families, but I think that it is better for children to begin formal lessons later. Before that age, they should have a lot of time to play, explore and enjoy their childhood. Parents and teachers should therefore not hurry children into the classroom.
